alex (DevEx): FYI — onboarding sample app 'todo-sync' just surfaced duplicated tasks when a user hits 429 during token refresh.

jamie (SDK): ugh. repro steps?

alex (DevEx): quick loop create, SDK auto-retry + background refresh -> two 201s. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:03:21Z] POST /v1/todos -> 201 id=abc123
[2026-03-10T14:03:21Z] token refresh started
[2026-03-10T14:03:21Z] POST /v1/todos -> 429 retrying
[2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] POST /v1/todos -> 201 id=def456
```

sara (Platform): is that endpoint supposed to be idempotent?

ajamie typo?

jamie (SDK): it's not. By default SDK retries on 429/5xx. If a token refresh happens, the in-flight request may be replayed with a new auth token and cause a duplicate create.

michael (eng-ml): sample app uses default SDK without Idempotency-Key.

alex (DevEx): proposal: SDK should offer optional deterministic idempotency-key generation for write ops and persist that key across retries/refreshes. Also add a lightweight `x-replay-guard` header servers can use to short-circuit duplicates.

jamie (SDK): agreed. prototype idea: generate idempotencyKey = sha256(method + path + body + client_nonce) and attach header. Ensure retries use same key.

alex (DevEx): example for docs:
```js
// node (pseudocode)
const idKey = opts.idempotencyKey || sha256(req.method + req.path + JSON.stringify(req.body) + clientNonce)
headers['Idempotency-Key'] = idKey
// store idKey on request context so auth refresh/replay uses identical key
```

sara (Platform): server-side needs a quick KV check (Redis) to detect existing idempotency keys and return the previous 201/200 payload or a 409 depending on semantics. We already have a small lease implementation for uploads; could reuse pattern.

jamie (SDK): backoff policy note: current SDK uses linear jitter for some flows. We should switch to full jitter (exponential base with uniform random) for bursty 429s. Default: base=100ms cap=8s retries=5.

michael (eng-ml): what about idempotency window? 30s? 60s? needs to balance memory and user-visible duplicates.

sara (Platform): start with 30s for onboarding sample app; we can tune per-route later. We'll emit metrics for idempotency hits/misses.

alex (DevEx): practical next steps:
- SDK: add "autoIdempotency" opt-in flag + deterministic key generation and ensure key survives token refresh.
- Platform: add Redis idempotency check and `x-replay-guard` enforcement.
- DevEx: update todo-sync README and onboarding doc to opt-in for safe-replay mode and show how to supply idempotency keys.

jamie (SDK): I'll open a small PR with a toggle: `autoIdempotency: true/false` and env var `REDWOOD_SDK_AUTO_IDEMP`. Default to false for now so existing contracts don't change unexpectedly.

alex (DevEx): can we enable it in the sample app though? New users should see safe defaults.

jamie (SDK): yes, sample app will enable the flag and include a comment explaining rationale.

michael (eng-ml): QA: I'll write a stress test that simulates token refresh mid-flight and assert we create <=1 item per logical request.

alex (DevEx): filing small follow-up: DEVEX-879 (onboarding replay protection).

jamie (SDK): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/575 — includes deterministic key and backoff change.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-10 14:20:00 started for branch sdk/replay-guard

jamie (SDK): I'll ping reviewers in an hour.

sara (Platform): I'll prototype the Redis check and post a design doc in #platform-arch.

alex (DevEx): thanks all — updating sample app and docs now. :rocket:
